Stretch Marks Treatment in Jaipur | Laser, MNRF & Microneedling

Stretch marks treatment makes red or white stretch marks softer, flatter and less noticeable by helping the skin rebuild collagen. Fractional laser, microneedling with radiofrequency (MNRF), microneedling and PRP are the main options, often combined. At Kezza, stretch marks are assessed and treated by our doctors at our Jaipur, Sikar and Ajmer clinics.

The Condition

What Are Stretch Marks?

Stretch marks are a type of scar that forms when the skin stretches or shrinks quickly, for example during pregnancy, growth spurts or weight change. Treatment cannot make them disappear completely, but fractional laser, microneedling with radiofrequency and PRP can make them softer, flatter and less noticeable, usually over three to six sessions.

When skin is stretched faster than it can adapt, the collagen and elastic fibres in its middle layer tear. Early stretch marks look red, purple, pink or dark brown, depending on your skin tone, and they may itch. Over months they fade to white or silvery lines that sink slightly below the surface. Doctors call them striae distensae: striae rubrae when they are new and striae albae when they are older.

They are most common on the tummy, breasts, hips, thighs, buttocks, upper arms and back. Pregnancy, puberty, gaining or losing weight quickly and rapid muscle growth from weight training are the usual causes. Steroid creams or tablets used for a long time can also cause them, and rarely they are a sign of a hormone condition such as Cushing's syndrome.

Early, coloured stretch marks respond better than old white ones, which remain the hardest to treat. Research on stretch marks shows that every method works for some people and less for others, so plans combine treatments and aim for a realistic improvement rather than complete removal.

In Short:

  • Early is easier: red marks respond better than white ones.
  • Combination plans: laser, MNRF, microneedling and PRP.
  • Realistic aim: softer, flatter, less visible marks.
Treatment Options

Stretch Mark Treatments at Kezza

Microneedling RF (MNRF)

Fine needles deliver radiofrequency heat into the skin to rebuild collagen, with a lower risk of dark marks than strong lasers.

Fractional CO2 Laser

Creates tiny columns of controlled injury that trigger new collagen, used at settings chosen for your skin type.

Microneedling

Collagen induction with fine needles, which works across skin types and is often combined with PRP.

PRP

Platelet-rich plasma from your own blood, added to microneedling or laser to support healing and collagen growth.

Creams for Early Marks

Prescription retinoid creams can help new red marks, outside pregnancy and breastfeeding.

Combined Plans

Treatments are matched to the colour, age and depth of your marks, and to your skin type.

Suitability

Is Stretch Mark Treatment Right for You?

Most adults with stretch marks can be treated, but timing matters.

Treatment may suit you if

  • You have stretch marks on your tummy, hips, thighs, breasts, arms or back
  • Your marks are red, pink or purple, or have faded to white or silver
  • You have finished pregnancy and breastfeeding, or your weight has been steady for a few months
  • You want them to look softer and less noticeable, and understand they will not disappear completely

Wait, or see a doctor first, if

  • You are pregnant or breastfeeding: procedures and retinoid creams are planned for afterwards
  • New, wide, purple stretch marks appear with weight gain on your trunk, a round red face or easy bruising
  • You have used steroid creams on the area, which can cause stretch marks and need stopping under advice
  • You have a skin infection or rash in the area, or tend to form raised (keloid) scars
  • You have taken isotretinoin recently; your doctor will advise how long to wait

Darker skin can develop temporary dark patches after laser or microneedling. Settings, spacing between sessions and skin preparation are chosen with this in mind.

Procedure

How a Stretch Mark Session Works

Most plans involve a course of sessions spaced a few weeks apart.

01

Assessment

The doctor looks at how old and how deep your marks are, asks about pregnancy, weight changes, medicines and creams, and takes photos, with your consent, to compare later.

02

Your Plan

You agree on the treatment or combination, the number of sessions and the gap between them, and the cost.

03

Numbing

A numbing cream is applied to the area for comfort before treatment.

04

Treatment

The chosen device is passed over the marks in a planned pattern; PRP, if used, is applied or injected during the session.

05

Aftercare & Review

You get aftercare advice for the next few days, and progress is checked with photos every few sessions.

Timeline

Stretch Mark Treatment Timeline

Collagen rebuilds slowly, so the full result shows months after the last session.

D1

Treatment Day

The area looks red and feels warm, like mild sunburn; you can go home straight away.

D4

First Few Days

Redness settles over a few days to a week; after laser there may be fine scabs or flaking.

W4

Every Three to Six Weeks

The next session is booked once the skin has fully settled.

M3

Around Three Months

Marks start to look flatter and less shiny as new collagen forms.

M6

Months After the Course

Texture and colour keep improving; the result is judged a few months after the last session.

Medical Note: Results vary from person to person. This page is general information from Kezza Hair & Skin Clinic and is not a substitute for a consultation with a doctor.

Red and white stretch marks need different plans

New stretch marks still have colour because of inflammation and blood vessels in the healing skin. At this stage, prescription retinoid creams such as tretinoin have improved early marks in studies, and collagen-building treatments tend to work better than they will later. Lasers that target redness are used for red marks in some countries, but they are not recommended for darker skin types, so for most Indian skin the focus is on microneedling radiofrequency, microneedling and gentle fractional laser. Old white marks have thin, flat collagen and few pigment cells. They need treatments that rebuild the skin's structure, and even then the change is gradual. Peels with glycolic acid combined with tretinoin, and microdermabrasion, can help the surface texture alongside these procedures.

How the treatments compare

TreatmentBest forRecovery
Microneedling RF (MNRF)Most skin types; red and white marksRedness for a few days; more discomfort during treatment
Fractional CO2 laserDeeper, textured or white marksMore redness and flaking; higher risk of dark marks in darker skin
MicroneedlingEarly and white marks; all skin typesRedness for a few days to a week
PRPAdded to other treatmentsLittle extra downtime

In an Indian trial of 98 people treated with four sessions three weeks apart, fractional CO2 laser gave excellent improvement in more people than microneedling with PRP, but it also caused more redness and darkening. That trade-off is why the choice depends on your skin type and how much downtime you can manage.

Stretch marks after pregnancy

Stretch marks affect many women in pregnancy, most often on the tummy, breasts and thighs. During pregnancy and breastfeeding, cosmetic procedures and retinoid creams are usually postponed, and gentle moisturising is the safest option for itchy skin. Once breastfeeding has finished and your weight has settled for a few months, the marks can be assessed and treated. Marks that still look pink or brown at that point usually respond better than those that have already turned white.

Do creams and oils prevent stretch marks?

Many products claim to prevent stretch marks, but the evidence does not support them. A Cochrane review of six trials involving about 800 pregnant women found no high-quality evidence that any cream or oil prevents stretch marks, and studies of almond oil, cocoa butter, olive oil and vitamin E have not shown that they fade existing marks. Gradual weight change, gaining pregnancy weight within your doctor's advice and avoiding unprescribed steroid creams are more useful steps. Moisturisers can still make dry, itchy skin more comfortable.

Why patients choose Kezza for stretch marks

  • Honest expectations: the doctor explains how much improvement is realistic for marks of your age and colour before you start.
  • Settings for your skin: energy levels and the gap between sessions are chosen to lower the risk of dark marks in Indian skin.
  • Combined plans: MNRF, laser, microneedling and PRP are combined when that suits your marks better than one method alone.
  • Three clinics: Jaipur, Sikar and Ajmer, open 9 AM to 8 PM every day.
  • Clear costs: the number of sessions and the total cost are explained at your consultation.

What affects the cost of stretch marks treatment?

The cost depends on the size and number of areas treated, the method or combination chosen and the number of sessions you need. A small area of early marks usually needs fewer sessions than large areas of older white marks. Your doctor explains the plan and the total cost before treatment.

FAQs

Frequently Asked Questions

Can stretch marks be removed completely?
Not usually. The NHS notes that stretch marks fade over time but may not disappear completely, and the American Academy of Dermatology describes them as permanent but able to become less noticeable with treatment. The aim is softer, flatter marks that blend better with the skin around them.
Which treatment works best for white stretch marks?
White marks are the hardest to improve. Treatments that rebuild collagen, such as microneedling radiofrequency, fractional laser and microneedling, often combined with PRP, give the most consistent improvement. Your doctor chooses between them based on your skin type and the depth of the marks.
How many stretch mark sessions will I need?
Most people need three to six sessions, spaced three to six weeks apart, depending on the method and how old the marks are. Studies of microneedling and laser for stretch marks typically use four or more sessions.
Is laser treatment safe for stretch marks on Indian skin?
It can be, when used with care. Darker skin is more prone to burns and dark marks after laser treatment, especially at high energy or density, so settings are kept conservative and the skin is prepared beforehand. Microneedling radiofrequency is often chosen because its risk of dark marks is lower.
Can I have stretch mark treatment while breastfeeding?
Procedures are usually planned after pregnancy, and retinoid creams are avoided while pregnant or breastfeeding. Ask your doctor; many people start treatment once breastfeeding has finished and their weight has settled.
Do stretch marks fade on their own?
The colour usually fades over months to years, from red or purple to a paler white or silver, but the change in skin texture tends to stay. Treating marks while they still have colour gives the best chance of improvement.
Does cocoa butter or almond oil prevent stretch marks?
There is no good evidence that they do. A Cochrane review of trials in pregnancy, including olive oil and cocoa butter, found no high-quality evidence that any cream or oil prevents stretch marks. Moisturisers can still help itchy, dry skin feel more comfortable.
Are stretch marks a sign of a health problem?
Usually not. They are very common after pregnancy, puberty and weight changes. Rarely, wide purple stretch marks with weight gain around the tummy and chest, thin arms and legs or a round red face can be caused by Cushing's syndrome, and long-term steroid use can also cause them. See a doctor if you notice these signs.
